_why_json: Stored as JSON, not as .html/.snapshot siblings, so the exact bytes survive any writer: inside a JSON string a newline is held as an escape sequence, not as a raw line break, so no write path can translate line endings underneath the snapshot and the probe can compare raw with nothing able to normalise a real change out of sight. The rancidity mechanism

The antioxidant that keeps your cells from going rancid

01
Your cells are fat
Every cell and every mitochondrion is wrapped in a membrane made of fat — and fat oxidizes, goes rancid, the same way cooking oil does once it's heated or left out.

The rancidity that spoils oil in the pan can happen inside your own cell walls.

02
The most efficient antioxidant
Selenium — working through the glutathione-peroxidase enzyme system — is, in Wallach's telling, the most efficient antioxidant there is, standing guard over those fatty membranes right at the subcellular level.

A trace mineral you need in millionths of a gram is the bodyguard on every membrane you own.

03
Rancid, made visible
Pull selenium out and the fats peroxidize — the brown-gold residue (ceroid lipofuscin) surfaces on skin as "age spots" or "liver spots," while selenium-starved heart muscle can fail outright, as in Keshan disease and the sudden collapse of young athletes.

An age spot is rancid fat you can see — Wallach reads it as a warning, not a blemish.

Selenium prevents cellular and subcellular lipids and fats from being peroxidized which literally means it prevents body fats from going rancid (seen externally as “age spots” or “liver spots” - this brown gold peroxidized lipid is known as ceroid lipofuscin).

sections.copper:
One cofactor · two endings

The same shortage shows up in your mirror and in your arteries.

The one you can see

Copper is the cofactor for tyrosinase — the enzyme that works on tyrosine to make the melanin that colours hair. Whatever your natural colour, short the copper and the pigment stops being made: it grows back white, grey or silver.

The one you can’t

Copper is also the cofactor for lysyl oxidase — the enzyme that converts pro-elastin into the elastin that gives an artery wall its tensile strength. Short the copper and the wall gives where the pressure is highest.

The first thing you’d notice
Copper deficiency in human beings presents itself first as white, gray, or silver hair.Dead Doctors Don't Lie (3rd ed. 2011)
Of every 100 Americans autopsied
4–6 had died of a ruptured aneurysm
40 carrying one, not yet ruptured — Wallach names Einstein, Airola and Twitty

They don’t arrive together — and that is the whole point. The visible one runs decades ahead of the silent one, which is what makes grey hair worth reading rather than covering up.

First
Pigment goes
Tyrosinase needs copper to make melanin. Pigment is the first thing to fail — and the first thing you can see.
Then
Structure goes
The same shortage, further along. Elastin thins: skin wrinkles deeply, spider and varicose veins surface, and artery walls lose the tensile strength that keeps them from ballooning.
After
Copper restores it
Wallach reports the sequence running in reverse on plant-derived colloidal copper — original hair colour returning, veins receding, and some aneurysms healing.

When humans supplement with plant derived colloidal copper, their original hair color can come back, spider veins, varicose veins, and hemorrhoids can go away and some aneurysms can heal.

sections.vitamin-a:
One vitamin · two very different forms

A carrot doesn’t hand you vitamin A — only the raw material.

what a carrot’s label calls “Vitamin A”
Vitamin A*

* really β-carotene — a precursor, not the vitamin.

+
Safe to mega-dose — it’s an antioxidant in its own form, so overdosing becomes nearly impossible.
−
Less convenient daily — your liver must convert it first (needs zinc), a less direct way to hit your target.
in liver · butter · egg
Vitamin A ✓

The active form — retinol.

+
Ready to use — the active form, so it’s the direct way to hit your daily target.
−
Toxic in excess — above about 50,000 IU a day, kept up over time.
In practice
Not better vs. worse — a difference in job. Because you almost can’t overdose on β-carotene, it’s the form Wallach doses at pharmacologic extremes — 300,000 IU, even 600,000 with vitamin E — to treat disease. Retinol turns toxic past ~50,000 IU, so it stays at everyday maintenance amounts — the small dose that meets your daily target.
Did you know?

A cure that arrived four thousand years early

Around 2000 BC, Egyptian healers treated night blindness by pressing beef-liver juice onto the eyes — not eating it — and it worked. Science took four thousand years to catch up: vitamin A wasn’t isolated until 1913, and only then did we learn the liver stores it and the eye is the first thing to fail without it. The Egyptians had no chemistry to find a vitamin hidden in fat, no way to link a liver to an eye — yet they went straight to it. It reads less like something worked out than something handed down — complete, and already correct.

Egyptian cure & vitamin-A liver storage — Wallach, Epigenetics (2014)

NIGHT BLINDNESS (xerophthalmia) is caused by a vitamin A deficiency which can be overt dietary deficiency, fat malabsorption syndrome (vitamin A is fat soluble), zinc deficiency which results in poor conversion of carotene to vitamin A by the liver

— Dr. Joel Wallach · Dead Doctors Don't Lie (3rd ed. 2011)

sections.zinc:
What zinc actually does

Most nutrients are fuel. Zinc is a part.

Look at your own fingernails. Those little white spots almost everyone has? Wallach reads them as a sign you are short of zinc.

So why would a missing metal show up in a fingernail? Because zinc is not burned like fuel. It is built in.

That is the difference between fuel and a part. Run low on fuel and you feel tired. Lose a part and you feel nothing — a job just stops being done, and stays undone until the part is back.

01
Zinc holds the shape
An enzyme only works if it is the right shape to grip what it works on. Wallach says zinc is what holds that shape — take it out and the tool is still there, just fitting nothing.

It is not the fuel. It is the part.

02
Seventy tools take the same part
No fewer than seventy enzymes need zinc before they work at all. So one shortage does not stall one job — it stalls seventy.

One missing part, seventy tools.

03
One of them reads your DNA
A gene is an instruction for building something. Zinc sits inside the molecule that carries it, and the tool that reads it is a zinc tool too.

The instruction stays there, perfect, forever. Nothing can read it.

Which is why Wallach starts at a fingernail. Zinc is stored there, and he reads nails as a barometer of what you are absorbing.

// RARE EARTHS · ZINC METALLOENZYMES 70 tools that will not work until the part is back

Genetic engineers refer to the essential mineral cofactors as “metal fingers” which are required to activate genes!!! In the absence of the appropriate “metal finger” DNA and genes are powerless

— Dr. Joel Wallach · Rare Earths: Forbidden Cures (1st ed. 1994)
